
 Usage: openajar call [OPTIONS] {tool}

 Call any openajar tool from a shell, as your agents would: the same grant,
 policy and approvals.

 For an agent whose session has not loaded the openajar tools, and for scripts.

 Claude Code loads MCP servers only when a session starts. `openajar tools`
 lists the tools.

 Examples:

   openajar call environment

   openajar call environment_open --arg title=checkout --arg keep=none

   openajar call terminal_exec --on e7k2 --arg cmd="pnpm test"

   openajar call file_read --json '{"on": "e7k2", "path": "README.md"}'

 Prints the result as JSON. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 refused or failed, 2 still
 waiting for a person.

 For 2, approve it in the panel and run the same command again, or pass --wait.

╭─ Arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ *    tool      <str>  The tool's name, as `openajar tools` lists it (for     │
│                       example environment or terminal_exec).                 │
│                       [required]                                             │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --arg   -a      <str>    key=value; the value may be JSON (--arg limit=5,    │
│                          --arg 'params={"text": "hi"}').                     │
│ --json          <str>    All the arguments as one JSON object, or @file.     │
│ --on            <str>    The environment or lane the tool acts on (the `on`  │
│                          from environment_open, or workspace/name).          │
│ --wait          <float>  Seconds to wait when a person must approve first;   │
│                          once approved, the call runs again.                 │
│                          [default: 0.0]                                      │
│ --node          <str>    The connection to use (default: the only one).      │
│ --url           <str>    An MCP address instead of a connection, like        │
│                          http://127.0.0.1:7450, with the token in            │
│                          $OPENAJAR_TOKEN.                                    │
│ --help                   Show this message and exit.                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
